"'''XMAS'''" is a song by Australian singer [[Kylie Minogue]]. It was written by Duck Blackwell, Luke Fitton, [[Biffco|Richard Stannard]] and Minogue for the 2025 ''Fully Wrapped'' reissue of her first holiday album, ''[[Kylie Christmas]]'' (2015), with production by Blackwell and Stannard. An Amazon Music Original, it was released exclusively as a single through [[Amazon Music|Amazon's digital music store]] on 5 November 2025, with a physical release following on 12 December 2025. It was the [[UK singles chart]] [[List of UK singles chart Christmas number ones|Christmas number-one]] for 2025.

"XMAS" is a song by Australian singer Kylie Minogue. It was written by Duck Blackwell, Luke Fitton, Richard Stannard and Minogue for the 2025 Fully Wrapped reissue of her first holiday album, Kylie Christmas (2015), with production by Blackwell and Stannard. An Amazon Music Original, it was released exclusively as a single through Amazon's digital music store on 5 November 2025, with a physical release following on 12 December 2025. It was the UK singles chart Christmas number-one for 2025.

sections.heading: Development and writing
sections.wikitext:
"XMAS" was written by Minogue along with Duck Blackwell, Luke Fitton, and [[Biffco|Richard Stannard]], with production by Blackwell and Stannard.<ref name="Amazon"/> In an interview, Minogue stated that the song originated in 2015 during a summer visit to Soho House in [[Berlin]], shortly after completing work on ''[[Kylie Christmas]]''.<ref name="Billboard">{{cite magazine|last=Lynch|first=Jessica|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/kylie-minogue-holiday-single-xmas-1236124962/|title=Kylie Minogue Says Holiday Single 'XMAS' Was a Decade in the Making |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=1 December 2025 |access-date=9 December 2025}}</ref> Ideas for "XMAS" emerged on the club's terrace after "a couple of glasses of wine".<ref name="Billboard"/> The concept developed as a playful twist on American disco group [[Village People]]'s 1978 hit single "[[YMCA (song)|YMCA]]", reimagined as "XMAS", and the chorus remained unused for a decade before being revisited.<ref name="Billboard"/>

Ultimately, it was not released at the time, as it did not feel like the right fit for that project. The song remained unreleased while it underwent further development, with the creative team later revisiting it to ensure it aligned with Minogue's vision and felt contemporary for a 2025 release. Once completed and mastered, the track stood out internally for its immediate memorability, with its chorus described as "an instant earworm after only a single listen." Planning for the release of "XMAS" began approximately a year in advance, with the campaign developing steadily throughout 2025. From as early as January, the team set a clear objective of achieving both a Christmas number-one album and single, shaping the rollout strategy accordingly. Confidence in the song's prospects grew as preparations progressed, particularly after securing [[Amazon Music]] as a promotional partner.<ref name="musicweekinterview">{{cite news|url=https://www.musicweek.com/talent/read/we-always-had-our-eyes-on-the-prize-inside-the-triumphant-kylie-christmas-no-1-campaign-for-xmas/093295|title='We always had our eyes on the prize': Inside the triumphant Kylie Christmas No.1 campaign for XMAS|work=[[Music Week]]|date=19 December 2025|last=Paine|first=Andre|accessdate=20 December 2025}}</ref>

Recorded in three days between her 2025 [[Tension Tour]], Minogue remarked in an interview with [[Scott Mills]]'s ''Breakfast Show'' on [[BBC Radio 2]], that "XMAS" was the song she "needed to [exorcise]. I needed to get it out. It's been 10 years in the making."<ref name="independent">{{cite news|last=Garnsworthy|first=Jenny |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/news/kylie-minogue-christmas-album-anniversary-b2859067.html |title=Kylie Minogue announces 10th anniversary Christmas album featuring new song |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |date=5 November 2025 |access-date=9 December 2025}}</ref>
sections.text:
"XMAS" was written by Minogue along with Duck Blackwell, Luke Fitton, and Richard Stannard, with production by Blackwell and Stannard. In an interview, Minogue stated that the song originated in 2015 during a summer visit to Soho House in Berlin, shortly after completing work on Kylie Christmas. Ideas for "XMAS" emerged on the club's terrace after "a couple of glasses of wine". The concept developed as a playful twist on American disco group Village People's 1978 hit single "YMCA", reimagined as "XMAS", and the chorus remained unused for a decade before being revisited.

Ultimately, it was not released at the time, as it did not feel like the right fit for that project. The song remained unreleased while it underwent further development, with the creative team later revisiting it to ensure it aligned with Minogue's vision and felt contemporary for a 2025 release. Once completed and mastered, the track stood out internally for its immediate memorability, with its chorus described as "an instant earworm after only a single listen." Planning for the release of "XMAS" began approximately a year in advance, with the campaign developing steadily throughout 2025. From as early as January, the team set a clear objective of achieving both a Christmas number-one album and single, shaping the rollout strategy accordingly. Confidence in the song's prospects grew as preparations progressed, particularly after securing Amazon Music as a promotional partner.

Recorded in three days between her 2025 Tension Tour, Minogue remarked in an interview with Scott Mills's Breakfast Show on BBC Radio 2, that "XMAS" was the song she "needed to [exorcise]. I needed to get it out. It's been 10 years in the making."

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: ''[[Classic Pop]]'' editor Annie Zaelski called "XMAS" a "peppy synth pop" track and an "undeniable earworm", that was "leaning on tricks like spelling out catchphrases rather than more clever gambits".<ref name="Zaelski ">{{cite web|last=Zaelski |first=Annie|url=https://www.threads.com/@kylie.twst/post/DR2xmWjjdgf/media|title=Stop Press: Kylie Christmas (Fully Wrapped)|website=[[Classic Pop]] |via=[[Threads (social network)|Threads]]|access-date=9 December 2025}}</ref> Daniel Welsh of ''[[The Huffington Post]]'' found that "XMAS" was "a nice enough – though still pretty naff – festive ditty that will no doubt particularly appeal to little ones, leaning into trends laid out in recent hits for acts like [[Bruno Mars]] and [[Chappell Roan]], complete with its own [[TikTok dance]]." He argued, however, that it sounded like a boardroom-engineered bid for a chart hit.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Christmas Music 2025: Our Verdict On This Year's Must-Listen Festive Songs |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/new-christmas-songs-2025-our-reviews_uk_691dd149e4b06f2a60cadeea |access-date=19 December 2025 |website=[[Huffington Post]]}}</ref>
sections.text: Classic Pop editor Annie Zaelski called "XMAS" a "peppy synth pop" track and an "undeniable earworm", that was "leaning on tricks like spelling out catchphrases rather than more clever gambits". sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
"XMAS" debuted at number 64 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] in the week ending 4 December 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/20251128/7501/|title=Official Singles Chart Top 100: 28 November 2025 – 4 December 2025|publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=13 December 2025}}</ref> On 14 December 2025, the UK's [[Official Charts Company]] announced their midweek chart list, showing that "XMAS" was at the number one position, 7,000 copies ahead of the number two competitor, [[Wham!]]'s "[[Last Christmas]]" (1984), in the [[List of UK singles chart Christmas number ones|race for the 2025 Christmas number-one single]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/kylie-minogue-leads-official-christmas-number-1-single-xmas-together-for-palestine/|title=Kylie takes early lead in UK Christmas Number 1 race, but Together For Palestine, Wham! and The Pogues are hot on her tail|publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|last=Persad|first=Max|date=14 December 2025|accessdate=16 December 2025}}</ref> The song became Minogue's eighth UK number-one single overall and her first chart-topping single in twenty-two years after "[[Slow (Kylie Minogue song)|Slow]]" (2003). With this achievement, Minogue became the first woman to score UK number-one singles across four different decades (the 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, and 2020s) and the oldest female artist to have a number one with a new recording.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kylie Minogue scores first Christmas No.1 as Amazon exclusive XMAS finishes ahead of catalogue hits |url=https://www.musicweek.com/labels/read/kylie-minogue-scores-first-christmas-no-1-as-amazon-exclusive-xmas-finishes-ahead-of-catalogue-hits/093294 |access-date=2025-12-19 |website=www.musicweek.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name=YearinReview25>{{cite web|last= White|first= Jack|date= December 26, 2025|title= 2025 Music Year in Review: Reunions, record-breakers and a renaissance|url= https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/2025-music-moments-biggest/ | access-date=December 26, 2025|publisher=Official Charts Company}}</ref>

Selling 55,926 units during the week,<ref name="musicweekinterview"/> "XMAS" ended Wham!'s two-year reign at the top of the Christmas chart and made Minogue the first solo female artist to claim the Christmas number-one song in 12 years, as well as only the third international female solo artist ever to do so. The track is Amazon Music's first Christmas number-one and was the best-selling physical and vinyl single of the week, marking Minogue's biggest UK week for single sales and streams in over two decades.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/christmas-number-1-2025-kylie-minogue-xmas/|title=Christmas Number 1 2025: Kylie Minogue's XMAS breaks Official Chart records!|publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|last=Smith|first=Carl|date=19 December 2025|access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref> As of 19 December 2025, "XMAS" has sold 110,685 copies in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.musicweek.com/the-official-uk-singles-chart|title=Xmas appeal: Kylie notches her first ever Christmas chart-topper|publisher=Music Week|last=Jones|first=Alan|date=29 December 2025|accessdate=22 December 2025}}</ref>

In Australia, "XMAS" debuted at number 4 on the Australian Artist Singles chart.<ref name="cdn.aria.com.au">{{Cite web|url=https://cdn.aria.com.au/pdfs/455DA4191B43E489908A93FDE3A2A43F70585F919B8626924FFEFEB44259CF28/ARIA%20Australian%20Artist%20Singles%20Chart.pdf?seq=44|title= ARIA Australian Artist Singles Chart|date=22 December 2025|access-date=19 December 2025}}</ref>
sections.text:
"XMAS" debuted at number 64 on the UK Singles Chart in the week ending 4 December 2025. On 14 December 2025, the UK's Official Charts Company announced their midweek chart list, showing that "XMAS" was at the number one position, 7,000 copies ahead of the number two competitor, Wham!'s "Last Christmas" (1984), in the race for the 2025 Christmas number-one single. The song became Minogue's eighth UK number-one single overall and her first chart-topping single in twenty-two years after "Slow" (2003). With this achievement, Minogue became the first woman to score UK number-one singles across four different decades (the 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, and 2020s) and the oldest female artist to have a number one with a new recording.

Selling 55,926 units during the week, "XMAS" ended Wham!'s two-year reign at the top of the Christmas chart and made Minogue the first solo female artist to claim the Christmas number-one song in 12 years, as well as only the third international female solo artist ever to do so. The track is Amazon Music's first Christmas number-one and was the best-selling physical and vinyl single of the week, marking Minogue's biggest UK week for single sales and streams in over two decades. As of 19 December 2025, "XMAS" has sold 110,685 copies in the United Kingdom.

In Australia, "XMAS" debuted at number 4 on the Australian Artist Singles chart.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
[[Image:Vecrīga, Central District, Riga, LV-1050, Latvia - panoramio (200).jpg|thumb|Exterior scenes for "XMAS" were filmed at various locations in Riga's Old Town, including Mazā Pils Street.<ref name="filmneweurope"/>]]
Minogue reteamed with director [[Sophie Muller]] to film a [[music video]] for "XMAS".<ref name="filmneweurope">{{Cite web|first=Ieva |last=Lange|url=https://www.filmneweurope.com/news/latvia-news/item/127545-kylie-minogue-visited-riga|website=filmneweurope.com|title=Kylie Minogue Visited Riga|date=16 December 2025|access-date=19 December 2025}}</ref> Filming took place in late October 2025 in [[Riga]], Latvia, where the visuals for "Office Party" and "Hot in December" were also shot.<ref name="filmneweurope"/> While the interior scenes were filmed at the Riga Film Studio, exterior scenes for "XMAS" were shot at various locations in [[Riga Old Town]], including Mazā Pils Street.<ref name="filmneweurope"/> The video sees Minogue performing in a host of seasonal settings and features [[cameo appearance]]s by Minogue's younger sister [[Dannii Minogue|Dannii]], actress [[Naomi Watts]], and [[ABBA]] member [[Björn Ulvaeus]].<ref>{{Cite web|first=Michael|last=Imhof|url=https://www.schweizer-illustrierte.ch/people/international-stars/ist-kylie-minogue-die-neue-konigin-der-weihnacht-891870|website=[[Schweizer Illustrierte]]|title=Ist Kylie Minogue die neue Königin der Weihnacht?|date=17 December 2025|access-date=17 December 2025|language=German}}</ref> It premiered on 12 December 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Carl |last=Smith |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/kylie-minogue-xmas-music-video-christmas-number-1/|website=[[Official Charts Company]]|title=Kylie Minogue unleashes camp as Christmas XMAS music video|date=17 December 2025|access-date=19 December 2025}}</ref>
sections.text:
thumb|Exterior scenes for "XMAS" were filmed at various locations in Riga's Old Town, including Mazā Pils Street.
Minogue reteamed with director Sophie Muller to film a music video for "XMAS". Filming took place in late October 2025 in Riga, Latvia, where the visuals for "Office Party" and "Hot in December" were also shot. While the interior scenes were filmed at the Riga Film Studio, exterior scenes for "XMAS" were shot at various locations in Riga Old Town, including Mazā Pils Street. The video sees Minogue performing in a host of seasonal settings and features cameo appearances by Minogue's younger sister Dannii, actress Naomi Watts, and ABBA member Björn Ulvaeus. It premiered on 12 December 2025.
